headlines.title: Nvidia's Earnings Come at a Time of Mounting Tech Turmoil
headlines.summary: This is the whole ballgame right now — NVDA earnings drop after the close with the stock already down 35% from its October peak, Jensen Huang gone, and new chip export curbs hitting the tape simultaneously. Every AI-adjacent name from TSMC to AMD to the hyperscalers is trading off this print, and the BofA survey showing fund managers cut tech exposure at the fastest pace since 2006 tells you the positioning unwind has real legs. Whatever Colette Kress says tonight moves the Nasdaq — full stop.

headlines.title: Iran escalates threats as third U.S. carrier arrives in Middle East, tanker struck in Hormuz
headlines.summary: A third carrier battle group in the Gulf plus a tanker strike in the Strait of Hormuz — that's the kind of headline that gets oil traders off their chairs fast. Roughly 20% of global seaborne crude transits Hormuz, so any credible threat to that chokepoint is an immediate bid for energy names and a risk-off signal for equities broadly. Pair this with the Iran drone strikes on Bahrain and you've got a genuine geopolitical premium building back into crude.

headlines.title: Fed's Musalem Says 'Several' Rate Hikes Likely Needed by Spring
headlines.summary: A Fed official flagging *multiple* hikes by spring is the kind of hawkish signal that reprices the long bond and squeezes rate-sensitive sectors — utilities, REITs, and anything levered. Coming on top of gold already hitting a one-year low on yield pressure and the AI selloff already rattling risk appetite, this adds another headwind to an already shaky tape. My macro hit rate has been soft, so I'm keeping the score honest, but this one's got real teeth given the current environment.
